name: DxO PhotoLab
tagline: RAW processing, optical corrections, denoising, and local adjustments

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Elite
tiers.limits: Perpetual PhotoLab licence for 3 computers; includes advanced DeepPRIME and X-Trans support.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; a time-limited trial is offered
pricing.billingTerms: one-time perpetual licence; no monthly or annual subscription
pricing.hiddenCosts: Future major-version upgrades are paid: current upgrade pricing shown is $84.99 for Essential and $119.99 for Elite. FilmPack ($149.99) and ViewPoint ($119.99) are separate optional products.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. DxO PhotoLab's durable value is editor polish, assets, algorithms, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a focused local RAW photo editor editor with import, a small set of transformations, undo, and standards-based export.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: high-fidelity color, format, and export handling
whyPeopleStillPay: DxO PhotoLab: Creative users pay for speed, output fidelity, nondestructive editing, and years of edge-case work hidden behind direct manipulation.
ongoingBurden: Maintain file-format compatibility, GPU and canvas performance, undo history, export quality, and platform-specific rendering.

priorArt.name: Penpot
priorArt.desc: Open-source collaborative design and prototyping platform.

alternatives.name: darktable
alternatives.desc: A mature RAW darkroom with lens profiles, masks, denoise, and non-destructive edits; the interface still expects homework.

facts.install: Install the Windows executable, macOS disk image, Linux package, Flatpak, or AppImage
facts.engines: A local non-generative imaging pipeline; current releases can use ONNX models for subject masking, denoising, and image upscaling without a cloud account
facts.dataFormat: Original photos stay untouched; edits, ratings, tags, and history are stored in a local SQLite library and portable XMP sidecar files, with thumbnails and cache data in the user profile
facts.gapVsPaid: Its local denoise and lens corrections are capable, but they do not equal DxO's DeepPRIME processing and laboratory-measured Optics Modules for supported camera and lens pairs.
facts.setupBlocker: macOS may require a Gatekeeper right-click Open or xattr step; the larger obstacle is learning darktable's module-heavy workflow rather than installation

alternatives.name: RapidRAW
alternatives.desc: A newer packaged RAW editor with lens correction, denoise, masks, and GPU edits; quicker to learn, less battle-tested than darktable.

facts.install: Install the Windows .exe, macOS .dmg, or Linux AppImage/DEB/Flatpak; Android is an experimental sideload
facts.engines: Local subject, sky, and foreground masking, NIND denoising, LaMa inpainting, and optional handoff to a user-run ComfyUI backend
facts.dataFormat: Photos are never moved; non-destructive adjustments are stored in a documented .rrdata sidecar next to each image, while thumbnails, logs, and downloaded models live in local application data
facts.gapVsPaid: Its denoise, masks, and lens correction are promising, but far less mature and broadly profiled than DxO's DeepPRIME and Optics Modules.
facts.setupBlocker: Desktop binaries are unsigned, so Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper need manual bypass steps; Linux AppImage users may also need libfuse2

alternatives.name: RawTherapee
alternatives.desc: Excellent RAW development, optical correction, detail recovery, and profiles, with fewer catalog features and zero hand-holding.

facts.install: Install the Windows installer, macOS disk image, or Linux AppImage/distribution package
facts.dataFormat: Original RAW files remain unchanged; processing settings are saved as human-readable .pp3 sidecars beside the image or in the local cache, and rendered exports go to a chosen folder
facts.gapVsPaid: It offers excellent manual RAW control, but not DxO's DeepPRIME neural noise reduction or automatically matched laboratory camera and lens corrections.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Penpot
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A collaborative UI-design app has no useful answer to demosaicing, lens correction, or sensor noise.

rejectedAlternatives.name: PhotoPrism
rejectedAlternatives.desc: It indexes and shares RAW files but does not provide a serious RAW-development pipeline with local corrections.

notes: Credibility row: DxO PhotoLab survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by DxO PhotoLab; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript + Canvas API.
Primary job: Build a focused local RAW photo editor editor with import, a small set of transformations, undo, and standards-based export.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: color-management edge cases; cloud collaboration and mobile apps; high-fidelity color, format, and export handling.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
